claims.claim: EU house prices rose 4.7 percent year on year in the second quarter of 2026, above inflation of 3.2 percent, according to Eurostat figures cited by Euronews Business.

claims.claim: Nine of 29 European nations posted double-digit annual house-price gains, led by Portugal at 16.5 percent and Bulgaria at 15.5 percent.

claims.claim: Spain’s house prices rose 12.1 percent, Italy’s 4 percent and Germany’s 0.6 percent.

claims.supporting_quote: Within the EU's Big Four economies, Spain was notable with a 12.1% increase, while Italy at 4% was under the EU average. Germany posted just a minor gain of 0.6%, slightly above France.

claims.claim: House prices fell year on year in Finland by 2.7 percent, Luxembourg by 2.2 percent and France by 0.8 percent.
